entries.gave: Read the Cut, docs/product-vision.md as it stands, and the three Mores kept; no inputs. The vision is for the accountant, who prints a client invoice with invoicer command, the installer, who sets that command up on the accountant machine, and invoicer maintainers, who weigh each change against O1 and O2.
Read product-vision best-practice.md and its template.md, and refactor-doc best-practice.md, to their end before any change.
The job, as the Cut decides it at N1 decision 0: invoicer gives the accountant a command that prints a client invoice from the spreadsheet lines at that client tax rate.
Roles named by their job, as N1 decision 2 gives them: accountant, one who prints a client invoice; installer, one who sets up the command on each accountant machine.
The accountant job gets done only once the installer sets the command up, so the installer stays a role, as N1 decisions 1 and 2 hold.
No person left whose job is unclear; the Cut decides both, so nothing to ask.
No split: every accountant counts a printed correct invoice as the job done, and every installer a machine where the command runs.
No merge: accountant and installer count different results as their job done.
Two roles, so neither is named user.
O1 and O2 as N2 decisions 0 and 1 give them, each with its role as the subject.
O1 ends at each client sent a correct invoice, and O2 at a machine ready to print, each an end in the role own work, not what the product does.
O1 and O2 stay distinct: an installer can finish a setup that no accountant yet prints with.
Tasks as N4 decision 0 gives them: O1 from the spreadsheet lines and rate to the printed invoice; O2 from a bare machine to the command running for the accountant.
KR1.1 counts failures only on machines where the command runs, needing help or with a wrong total; KR2.1 counts setups after which the command does not run, as N4 decision 1 gives.
KR1.2 the time from opening the spreadsheet to the printed invoice, the accountant own time included; KR2.2 the installer time from starting a setup to the command running.
Each key result says Lower is better.
Within each objective KR1 before KR2, stated once in the template ranking line as KR1.1 and KR2.1, which the template pattern allows; no rank notes on the key result lines.
No targets; the template line on Goodhart law carries the reason.
Pieces of work, from N5 decision 0: the invoice command, the README part for the accountant, the README setup section; and the three Concept ideas.
The command and the README accountant part serve O1; the README setup section serves O2; each idea serves O1, as N6 decision 3 gives.
The README setup section serves O2 without O1, and the README accountant part O1 without O2, so the two objectives stay apart.
No piece names two objectives now: each idea is marked for O1 alone, whose role meets it at every print, and a setup failure counts under KR2.1 alone.
Every piece serves an objective, so nothing to ask.
The person already gave the one way and the ideas, held in N6 decisions 0 and 1, so not asked again.
The one way in one sentence that goes on from the product: invoicer command prints the finished invoice from the spreadsheet invoice lines, plus the client tax rate.
Three ideas from the person, each with what it gives the accountant toward O1: no new format, nothing wrong prints, the rate given each time.
Moments as N6 decision 2 gives them: the installer sets up the command and sees it run; the accountant gives the lines and the rate; the invoice prints, or a message says what to fix.

Each moment has an idea that keeps the one way: setup needs nothing configured since the sheet stays as it is and the rate comes each time; giving the lines holds by the sheet as it is; the outcome by nothing wrong prints.
No idea proposed beyond the person three, so nothing to ask.
All three ideas kept: taking any out leaves a moment where the one way fails, a new format, a wrong invoice, or a stale rate.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end. Roles says who comes to invoicer; Objectives and key results says what each achieves and how a change is judged; Concept says the one way and its ideas.
Readers from the Cut name: the accounting team, who check what invoicer lets them do, and invoicer maintainers, who weigh each change against O1 and O2; installers read the installer lines.
The accountant knows invoices, tax rates and spreadsheets, not commands or OKR labels; a maintainer knows the code and comes to learn whom it serves and how a change is judged.
The three template sections each hold one topic; no split, as the template fixes the sections.
Each role, objective, key result and idea stands as its own list item with its label, so it shows and can be pointed to; no heading added beyond the template.
Roles, objectives with key results, and ideas are items in no order, as bulleted lists; the ranking line and the no-targets line are the template fixed prose.
Readers words from the person, held in the Cut: invoice lines, spreadsheet, tax rate, client, accounting team, developer, set up, print.
Words chosen from those: prints an invoice, not the print; help, not a developer help; sets up, not installs Python; the O and KR labels stay as the template fixes them.
Facts stated twice: the accountant installs nothing, once in the installer line only; the rate each time, once in its idea only; the ranking, once in the ranking line.
Each such fact stays in the one place named, its section topic.
No two places state a fact differently, so nothing to ask.
Names grouped: invoicer and invoicer command for what prints; a developer help and help for the help O1 means; accountant, installer; spreadsheet and sheet.
Kept, by N1 decision 3: invoicer command for what prints, invoicer for the product alone, help for any help, spreadsheet, accountant and installer.
No name left for two things once invoicer names only the product.
Took each of the 13 decisions of the Cut as it stands; settled without asking the wording that fits the 20-word sentence limit and the template line forms; no point left to ask.
O1 and O2 read with invoicer taken out still name ends: a correct invoice sent, a machine ready to print; neither reads as a feature.
Python taken out of the installer line, which now says only that the installer sets up the command so the accountant installs nothing; no sentence names a runtime or how the command works inside.

An E2E run records for KR1.1 each invoice on a set-up machine that needed help or had a wrong total; for KR1.2 the spreadsheet opened and the invoice printed; for KR2.1 whether the command runs after setup; for KR2.2 setup start and the command first run.

At setup, whether the installer configures rates or a sheet format: the one way and its ideas decide none, since the sheet is taken as it is and the rate comes each time; at a bad line, print nothing, as its idea says.
Headings Roles, Objectives and key results, Concept are the template fixed headings, kept as they are.
First lines under each heading are the template form, a role item, an objective item, the one way; not reworded, as the person chose to keep the template fixed sentences.
Read only the headings and first lines as the accountant and as a maintainer; each finds who it serves, its objectives, and the one way without a section skipped wrongly.
Every sentence has a reader: roles and ideas for the accountant and installer, key results and ranking for the maintainers; Python marked as needed by no reader of the vision.
Installing Python belongs to the README setup section, whose readers are installers, as N1 decision 3 says.
The README lies outside docs/product-vision.md, so nothing moved into a document of this deliverable.
No ask needed: the person already placed installing Python in the README setup section, kept in N1 decision 1 and its grounds for the README.
Cut installing Python and invoicer in place of the accountant from the installer line.
Words cut: further words of the ideas, such as Neither the accountant nor the installer; each kept word carries a step, value, or condition.
Articles, that, and as kept in each sentence.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end as the accountant, the installer and a maintainer; each still finds the step, value or condition their purpose needs.
Roles come before the objectives that name them, and the one way before the ideas that carry it; the accountant meets the command in Roles before KR1.1 names it.
No sentence depends on something outside the document; Goodhart law comes with its plain reason in the template line.
Sentences start with the known, such as the accountant, and end with the new, such as no new format or the line or value to fix.
Conditions lead: where the command runs in KR1.1, and for an unreadable line or rate in the second idea.
No rule with an exception in the vision.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end from the top; no place needed a look back or ahead beyond the template labels O and KR, which the template fixes.
Each role, objective, key result and idea stays one list item.
No sequence to draw: the vision states no steps passed between parts.
No structure to draw, as the vision leaves the parts to the architecture.
Each written sentence makes one point; the template ranking and no-targets lines left as the person chose.
Actors as subjects with active verbs: the accountant learns, gives; the command prints, takes, remembers.
Pronouns checked: they refers to the accountant only, none refers to the rate within five words.
Nouns from verbs kept only where the template sets them, such as setup in KR2.1 and KR2.2.
Each object sits next to its verb, such as prints the finished invoice, gives the client tax rate.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end word by word as a machine translator; each written sentence reads one way.
Words replaced: a developer help became anyone help and someone help; sheet became spreadsheet; installing Python became sets up the command.
No term of my own to define; O and KR labels come from the template, which the person chose to keep.
Abbreviations O and KR stand as the template sets them; E2E appears nowhere in the vision.
Each fact stated in full in its one section: who installs in Roles, measures in Objectives and key results, the rate rule in Concept.
No second place left that restates a fact, so no link needed; the third idea no longer restates that the installer sets up no rates.
invoicer prints replaced by invoicer command prints in the one way and the ideas; invoicer stands alone only in the title; each name in code format the same way each time.

docs/product-vision.md made: Python out of the installer line, KR1.1 counts only where the command runs, each idea marked for O1 alone, no developer in O1 and KR1.1, and invoicer command is what prints throughout.

Tried in a throwaway copy: template.py product-vision on the vision exits 0 with no fault; a search finds no Python, no idea marked for O2, and developer only in the installer role line, as N1 decision 2 gives.
